chunks: Then he had a long conversation with them (peace be upon him)

Among the things he said was: Did you not say when they raised the Qur'ans - as a stratagem and a trick, and deception and fraud - 'They are our brothers and our comrades in calling [to Islam]. They have asked us to cease [fighting] and have found rest in the Book of Allah, Glorified is He. So the opinion is to accept from them and to relieve them [of fighting]'?

So I said to you: 'This matter has an outward appearance of faith, but an inward reality of enmity. Its beginning is mercy, and its end is regret. So remain steadfast on your position, and adhere to your path, and press your teeth [in effort] in jihad, and do not pay heed to the caller who calls: If he is answered, he will mislead; and if he is left [unanswered], he will be disgraced.'
And this action [of arbitration] has taken place, and I have seen you agreeing to it.

key_terms.الْفَعْلَةُ: The action/deed (referring to the specific act of Arbitration)
key_terms.الْقَبُولُ: Acceptance (referring to accepting the terms of arbitration)
key_terms.الْمَصَاحِف: The Qur'ans (plural of Sahifa, referring to copies of the Qur'an raised for arbitration)
key_terms.نَوَاجِذ: Canines/Teets (used idiomatically for pressing teeth in effort/steadfastness)

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's assessment of the Arbitration event and his advice to the companions?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) critiques the companions' acceptance of the Quraysh-appointed arbitrators as a strategic concession that masked underlying enmity, contrasting their outward piety with the eventual regret of the Kharijites. He urges them to remain steadfast in their chosen path of jihad, dismissing the dissenters' cries as either misleading if answered or humiliating if ignored, thereby highlighting the political and theological complexities of the Siffin arbitration. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly view of the arbitration not merely as a military decision but as a pivotal moment of internal division and prophetic warning.
